memory_candidates.content: In this repo, scripts/typst-sync-check.sh Check 1 (backtick name resolution) only scans literal `` `name` `` backtick spans in typst/**/*.typ via regex -- it does not inspect #leansrc(module, name) macro call arguments at all. When documentation prose needs to name a Lean identifier that is a proposed next step and does not exist yet (e.g. a composite like `gQuot := sigmaQuot . hQuot . sigmaQuot` that is one definition away but unbuilt), write it in math notation ($sigma_"quot" compose H compose sigma_"quot"$) rather than backticks -- backticking a non-existent identifier fails Check 1 as an unresolved name, while math notation carries the same information without tripping the mechanical check or requiring a whitelist entry (which is reserved for genuine non-Lean nouns, not for proposed-but-unbuilt code).

When a research report's literature-index sub-index entries (specs/literature-index.json) lack full bibliographic metadata (year, venue, publisher) because they were registered by 'reason' text rather than full ingestion, pull the missing metadata from the actual global-corpus PDF at ~/Projects/Literature/sources/{doc_id}/*.pdf via `pdfinfo` (CreationDate often narrows the year) and `pdftotext -f 1 -l 1` (title page) rather than relying on memory or the sub-index's summary text alone. Cross-check against the paper's own reference-list self-citations or 'Received by the editors' dates when the source PDF is a preprint/technical-report version rather than the final offprint. Follow this repo's existing bibliography.bib convention of adding `note = {verify before print}` when the exact venue/year is reconstructed this way rather than read directly off a published offprint.

When a Phase 1 claim-audit's planned bibliography-entry list turns out to include an entry that ends up uncited after drafting the later phases' prose (e.g. a source kept as a secondary/proxy reference), do not silently drop the bibliography entry to satisfy a 'no uncited key' verification bar -- instead find or create a genuinely honest, narrow place to cite it (a footnote naming the specific terminological or historical point the source actually supports), consistent with the source's role identified during research. Dropping the entry loses a legitimate citation opportunity; forcing an uncited entry into unrelated prose to satisfy the checker is dishonest. A one-sentence footnote is usually enough.
